questions.explain: Risk combines a vulnerability and the threat that can exploit it, often expressed as likelihood × impact.

questions.q: Which factor increases the likelihood that a vulnerability will be exploited?
options: Internet exposure and a public exploit
questions.explain: Exposure and the availability of a public exploit make exploitation much more likely.

questions.q: Which of the following are threat intelligence sources? (Select all that apply)
options: The codename of an attacker group
questions.explain: Sources are both internal and external. A mere group codename is not an actionable intelligence source.

questions.q: What is the role of CVSS?
options: Assign a unique identifier to a flaw
Produce a severity score from 0 to 10
questions.explain: CVSS measures severity; CVE is the identifier and CWE is the weakness type.

questions.q: Match each concept to its definition.
questions.explain: The three CVSS metric groups and the role of CVE are classic exam definitions.

questions.q: Two flaws: A = CVSS 9.8 on an isolated test bench; B = CVSS 7.5 on an internet-facing server with a public exploit. Which should be prioritized?
options: A, because the score is higher
B, because exposure and the public exploit increase risk
questions.explain: Priority depends on context: exposure, exploitability, and criticality outweigh the raw CVSS score alone.
